questions.heading: A Property Is a Rule Every Plan Must Obey, Checked Outside the Model
questions.stem: In this lesson, two properties compare floats from the solver within a tolerance named TOL. What value does the lesson give TOL?

options.says: The lesson sets TOL = 1e-3, because GridCap's money is whole $k.
The lesson sets TOL = 1e-3; a far smaller tolerance would fail on HiGHS's noise.
1e-5 is the size of HiGHS's noise; TOL = 1e-3 sits above it.
Right: above HiGHS's noise near 1e-5, and GridCap's money is whole $k.

questions.heading: Validity Properties Miss a Rule That Is Too Strict; a Witness Catches It
questions.stem: hypothesis_finds.py ran the properties against the precedence row that adds 1 to the lag. What witness did the failing case it printed carry?

options.says: The printed witness was {'P1': 2027, 'P4': 2027}; P2 took no part in it.
Right: P1 and its child P4 in 2027, which a lag of 0 allows; the broken row left P4 out, so never_worse_than_the_witness failed.
The printed witness was {'P1': 2027, 'P4': 2027}, both in 2027.
The printed witness funded P1 and P4; P2 and P3 were worth 0 and left out.

questions.heading: Fix the Seed, Bound the Examples, Pin What You Found
questions.stem: hypothesis_finds.py ran plan_obeys_every_rule against bug 3 again, with its shrunk case added as an @example. Which header and noted plan did that run print?

options.says: Right: the pinned case ran first and failed before anything was drawn, with both projects in 2028.
The noted plan was {'P1': 2028, 'P2': 2028}: the pinned case's 2027 budget is 0.
The run printed 'Failing explicit example': it failed on the pinned case before drawing anything.
The plan is right, but the header was 'Failing explicit example': no case was drawn.
